title: AMC Matador
summary: The AMC Matador was a mid- and full-size automobile produced by American Motors Corporation from 1971 to 1978. Initially positioned as a family car, it transitioned to a full-size platform in 1974. The model found use as a police vehicle and appeared in media, including a James Bond film. It was also marketed internationally and competed in NASCAR racing with factory support.

mechanisms.title: Platform transition and redesign
mechanisms.explanation: The first generation (1971–1973) used a mid-size platform with hardtop, sedan, and wagon body styles. The second generation (1974–1978) shifted to a full-size platform, introducing a new two-door coupe with a unique design that shared no panels with other body styles, featuring a fastback silhouette and flared fenders.

mechanisms.title: Marketing and naming repositioning
mechanisms.explanation: AMC renamed its intermediate models from 'Rebel' to 'Matador' to distance the line from counterculture connotations and appeal to family-oriented buyers. A 'What's a Matador?' ad campaign used self-deprecating humor to build consumer familiarity and dealership traffic.
